balance: Building around a card that is already packing its bags.

name: Golden Buzzer
historical_reference: The Golden Buzzer — one press, straight through, confetti
card_art: A huge gold button mid-slam, confetti frozen at the top of its arc
effect: Consumable (once per run): skip one town's requirement ENTIRELY — instant win, full rewards, confetti.
why_fun: Rare, unearned-feeling, delightful — exactly one free miracle per tour.
balance: Spent on a show you could have won, it is the most expensive confetti alive.

name: Deus ex Machina
historical_reference: The Greek crane god — criticized as a cheat for 2,400 years, still hired
card_art: A golden crane arm lowering a serene figure into a collapsing finale
effect: Consumable (once per run): when a show is LOST, it is instead won at exactly goal (the god descends; the plot resolves). Deliberately feels like cheating.
pseudocode:
class ConsumableDeusEx extends BoosterTemplate:
  func use() -> void:  # usable at the loss screen
    game.state.total = game.state.goal
    game.override_outcome(WIN)
why_fun: The most honest name in the catalog — a cheat, labeled as a cheat, priced as a cheat.
balance: It saves one night, teaches nothing, and the next wall is taller.

name: The Major Arcana
historical_reference: The trionfi — trumps were a GAME for 300 years before the mystics arrived; Pamela Colman Smith drew the deck everyone knows and died uncredited
card_art: Twenty-two cards fanned in an arc, each glowing a different discipline
effect: Consumable SERIES: 22 unique one-shot consumables (Tower/Wheel/Hanged Man ship first; the rest follow) — collect all 22 across runs for a profile reward honoring the Uncredited Artist.
why_fun: Long-term chase content with a real ghost at the end — the artist finally credited.
balance: A collection spanning many runs; no single copy wins you anything tonight.

name: The Designated Loser
historical_reference: The Washington Generals — 13,000 losses; their 1971 win made children cry
card_art: A cheerful opposing troupe already rehearsing their bow
effect: Town hazard (morale node): a 'boss' show with a trivial goal you always beat... with a hidden 1-in-1000 (seeded) chance the Generals WIN — the goal silently triples mid-show.
why_fun: A guaranteed win that is not QUITE guaranteed — and the day it happens, the story is legendary.
balance: The one-in-a-thousand run that loses a freebie will not find it funny.

name: Lot Lice
historical_reference: 'Lot lice' — townsfolk who watched the setup for free
card_art: A row of spectators leaning on the fence, wallets conspicuously closed
effect: Town hazard: your FIRST submit each show scores 0 fame (they already watched for free).
why_fun: Compresses the show into two real acts — pacing pressure with a slang lesson.
balance: Effectively lose a third of the show; front-loaded decks suffer most.
status: remapped: act/Submit timing becomes the Entrance refill. See the post-grid effects CSV for the rewritten wording.

name: Mud Show
historical_reference: 'Mud show' — small circuses slogging unpaved roads between towns
card_art: Wagon wheels sunk to the axle, performers pushing in costume
effect: Town hazard: movement tax — every stack pickup this show costs 1 discard from the deck top.
pseudocode:
class HazardMudShow extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_can_grab_stack(stack) -> Variant:
    game.defer(func(): game.discard_from_deck_top())  # the toll
    return null  # legality unchanged; the mud just takes its cut
why_fun: Every rearrangement has a price tag — suddenly you play like a chess master.
balance: Fidgety players bleed their deck into the mud.

name: Knifetown's Snub
historical_reference: The user's Knifetown — unimpressed by knife scoring
card_art: A town square of crossed arms, every local wearing a knife
effect: Town hazard: Knives-suit effects score nothing here (they have seen knives).
pseudocode:
class HazardKnifetown extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_prop_passing(prop) -> Variant:
    if prop.kind == KNIFE: return NEGATE_PASS  # knives fly, pay zero
    return null
why_fun: The boss-blind resilience test, suit by suit — hyperfocus meets its bill.
balance: A knife-heavy deck plays this town half-blind.

name: Hooptown's Snub
historical_reference: The user's Hooptown
card_art: A town where every doorway, window, and dog collar is already a hoop
effect: Town hazard: Hoops-suit effects score nothing here.
pseudocode:
class HazardHooptown extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_prop_passing(prop) -> Variant:
    if prop.kind == HOOP: return NEGATE_PASS
    return null
why_fun: Same test, different church — the map keeps every archetype honest.
balance: Talent-sweep builds lose their engine at the gate.

name: Juggletown's Snub
historical_reference: The user's Juggletown
card_art: A juggling town — even the babies keep three rattles aloft
effect: Town hazard: Balls-suit effects score nothing here (Juggling statuses still apply, but pay 0).
pseudocode:
class HazardJuggletown extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_prop_passing(prop) -> Variant:
    if prop.kind == BALL: return NEGATE_PASS
    return null
why_fun: The setup suit gets snubbed — your deferred-value engine idles for one town.
balance: Juggling seeded here pays out only if you survive to the NEXT town.

name: Firetown's Snub
historical_reference: The user's Firetown
card_art: A town of smiths and chimneys, politely bored by flame
effect: Town hazard: Flames-suit effects score nothing here; Burning statuses do not multiply.
pseudocode:
class HazardFiretown extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_prop_passing(prop) -> Variant:
    if prop.kind == FIRE: return NEGATE_PASS
    return null
why_fun: The cascade build's cold shower — one town where fire is just warm.
balance: Burning stacks built here are pure wasted setup.

name: Temperance Town
historical_reference: Dry towns on the historical circus routes
card_art: A banner across Main Street: NO SPIRITS, NO SWEETS, NO NONSENSE
effect: Town hazard: Concessions-class cards disabled; shop prices doubled here.
pseudocode:
class HazardTemperance extends CardModifierSkill:  # temp rules_deck card
  func on_active() -> void:
    game.state.disabled_class = &'Concessions'
    run_state().shop_price_scale = 2.0
why_fun: A class ban that makes route planning matter — the sweet decks detour.
balance: Concessions decks lose healers AND face gouged prices in one stop.

name: The Fire Marshal
historical_reference: Post-1944 Hartford fire regulations reshaped tenting forever
card_art: A stern inspector holding a clipboard between a torch and a tent
effect: Town hazard: Flames-suit cards cannot score; any Flames card in your DECK is treated as Wax type this show.
why_fun: Regulation as a boss — the fire deck meets the one authority it cannot burn.
balance: Harsher than a snub: your fire cards actively melt here.

name: John Robinson
historical_reference: 'John Robinson' — the backstage code for CUT THE SHOW SHORT
card_art: A stage manager drawing a finger across his throat, gently
effect: Elite hazard: shortened show — 2 submits instead of 3 (the goal does not shrink).
why_fun: One act stolen — every setup line in your deck gets audited for speed.
balance: Slow-build engines (Hunger Artist, Fireworks ramps) simply do not fit in two acts.
status: remapped: act/Submit timing becomes the Entrance refill. See the post-grid effects CSV for the rewritten wording.

name: The Hook
historical_reference: Amateur night's shepherd's crook — bad acts yanked mid-bow
card_art: A long crook emerging from stage left, already curled around an ankle
effect: Town hazard: after each submit, your lowest-ranked board card is yanked (discarded) unless it scored that act.
why_fun: Every act must earn its slot — the crook keeps the whole roster honest.
balance: Glue cards (Blanks, tokens) get eaten exactly because they never score.
status: remapped: act/Submit timing becomes the Entrance refill. See the post-grid effects CSV for the rewritten wording.

name: Blowdown
historical_reference: Tent blowdowns — the traveling show's most feared weather
card_art: Canvas mid-collapse, ropes snapping, one lantern still lit
effect: Weather boss: at show start and each Next, a random (seeded) Grand Entrance card is discarded. The show must go on.
why_fun: The storm forces triage every single turn — protective stamps finally headline.
balance: Random loss punishes thin decks brutally; the Vine and Digital become gospel.

name: Hey Rube!
historical_reference: 'Hey Rube!' — the rallying cry when the circus fought the town
card_art: A brawl boiling at the tent flap, one performer mid-haymaker
effect: Boss: each submit, the rightmost column is ATTACKED — every card there gets Exhausted unless a Stuntsman/Strongman (Escape Artist class) stands in it.
why_fun: A geographic threat with a garrison mechanic — you post guards like a real lot boss.
balance: One column is conscripted all show; your Escape Artists become furniture.
status: remapped: act/Submit timing becomes the Entrance refill. See the post-grid effects CSV for the rewritten wording.

name: Railroad Jump
historical_reference: The brutal overnight railroad jumps of the golden age
card_art: A train receding into dark, one card left standing on the platform
effect: Route hazard (map edge): traveling this long edge costs one card from your deck — left on the platform (removed for the run).
why_fun: The route itself takes a toll — geography becomes a body count.
balance: Forced attrition; the long shortcut is never free.

name: The Volcano
historical_reference: The user's volcano note — performing near lava has consequences
card_art: A distant crater glow; the board's bottom row shimmering with heat
effect: Terrain boss: the bottom row of the Ring is LAVA — any card ending a turn there takes Burning and loses 1 rank per turn.
why_fun: The floor is literally lava — every column plans its own escape ladder.
balance: Deep columns must build UP fast or cook from below.

name: The Gong
historical_reference: The Gong Show — failure as the entertainment
card_art: An enormous brass gong, mallet already in motion, crowd delighted
effect: Town hazard: any submit scoring under a floor (25% of goal) ends the show IMMEDIATELY — the crowd loves the gong more than the acts.
why_fun: No sandbagging, no warm-up acts — every submit must clear the bar or the mallet falls.
balance: Setup acts (banking, seeding statuses) are exactly what gets gonged.
status: remapped: act/Submit timing becomes the Entrance refill. See the post-grid effects CSV for the rewritten wording.

name: The Prepared Town
historical_reference: Johnny Carson, ex-magician, controlled the props himself — nothing bent for Geller that night
card_art: A town square where every surface has been dusted for fingerprints
effect: Boss: pre-inspects everything — all Gaff/Humbug/fake/Masked cards are revealed and disabled for this show.
why_fun: The anti-fake audit every bluff deck fears — the town that did its homework.
balance: An honest deck walks through untouched; a Humbug deck arrives unemployed.

name: The Loggione
historical_reference: La Scala's gallery — connoisseurs who have booed the world's best off stage
card_art: A high balcony of opera glasses, all trained, none impressed
effect: Town hazard: Common cards score NOTHING here; Legendary cards score TRIPLE (the connoisseurs only rise for greatness).
why_fun: The anti-Kecak town — for one night, your deck's ceiling matters more than its floor.
balance: Commons-swarm decks meet a wall of folded arms.

name: Hall of Mirrors
historical_reference: The funhouse — distortion as delight
card_art: A boss board reflected wrong: familiar cards with unfamiliar smiles
effect: Boss: the show duplicates your board's reflection with FAKE copies of your cards (Gaffs) interleaved into rows — they score 0 and you must play around them.
why_fun: Fighting funhouse copies of your own deck — the boss is literally you, warped.
balance: Board space chokes fast; every meld must dodge your own reflections.

name: The Falling Wall
historical_reference: Buster Keaton, Steamboat Bill Jr. — the façade falls, the window saves him
card_art: A house wall mid-fall, one open window aligned with one calm card
effect: Boss attack (telegraphed one turn ahead): destroys an ENTIRE column except one exact row slot — stand your card in the window.
why_fun: The purest spatial-skill moment available — one turn to find the window, then the wall speaks.
balance: One column will be rubble; the question is only what stands in the frame.

name: The Rival Show
historical_reference: Circus wars — Barnum vs. Forepaugh, Ringling vs. everyone
card_art: Two big tops glaring at each other across one small town
effect: Recurring boss: a rival plays your town first — the goal arrives pre-raised 30%; BEAT it and steal one card from the rival's themed deck.
why_fun: Losing to them stings; ROBBING them afterwards is the whole revenge fantasy.
balance: The pre-raised goal lands whether or not your deck was ready for a war.

name: The Anarchist
historical_reference: Rejected as a player card (silencing the rule deck breaks everything) — reborn as the boss it always was
card_art: A grinning figure holding a lit match beside the rules deck
effect: Boss: each submit, ONE of your beneficial rule cards (Free Undo, Soundcheck, your added rules) is disabled for the rest of the show, in the order the Anarchist prefers.
why_fun: Your infrastructure crumbling one law at a time — the rule deck finally under siege.
balance: By act three the game you built is not the game you are playing.
status: vetoed by DESIGN_RECOMMENDATIONS 1: silencing the rule deck breaks the system everything runs on. Keep it as a blind, not a player card.

name: The Marathon
historical_reference: Depression-era dance marathons — endurance ground into spectacle
card_art: Exhausted couples still swaying under a WEEK 3 banner
effect: Boss gauntlet: a 3-show run where the board does NOT fully reset between shows (cards, statuses, and lava stay) and goals stack cumulatively.
why_fun: Consequences that survive the night — a three-show story your board tells in scars.
balance: Every mistake compounds for three shows; there is no clean morning.

name: The Balance
historical_reference: Barong vs. Rangda, Bali — the battle that neither side ever wins
card_art: A lion-spirit and a witch mid-eternal-clash, scales hanging level between them
effect: Final-tier boss: CANNOT be beaten by score — win by ending the show with row total and column total within 10% of each other (balance, not victory).
why_fun: The alt-win-con the design notes kept searching for — a boss that judges harmony, not size.
balance: Every number-go-up instinct you trained all run is suddenly the enemy.

name: Face cards count ten
effect: An optional rank rule where every face card counts as 10 for any summing meld - cribbage fifteens, the 20-30 row objective, the 31 count.
why_fun: Only matters once a summing meld exists; ships with The Fifteen and the rank-sum blinds.

name: Fifteens
effect: Any set of cards in one scored line summing to exactly 15 banks a flat bonus, once per distinct set.
why_fun: Cribbage's engine. Explicitly demoted from a default rule to an ability by a later draft line.

name: Thirty-ones
effect: Any set of cards in one scored line summing to exactly 31 banks a larger flat bonus.
why_fun: The blackjack-adjacent sibling of fifteens; rarer because 31 is harder to reach in five cards.

name: Pair meld
effect: Two cards of equal rank in a scored line. The floor of the poker table and the unit the pair-count blinds count.
why_fun: Already implemented by the poker evaluator; listed so blind objectives have a name to cite.

name: Triple meld
effect: Three of a kind in a scored line.
why_fun: Implemented.

name: Quad meld
effect: Four of a kind in a scored line - in a five-card line this leaves exactly one odd card.
why_fun: Implemented. The mahjong hands reuse this shape across a whole grid.

name: Run meld
effect: A consecutive rank sequence of three to seven cards. Lengths above five only exist on a long row spanning grids.
why_fun: The long-row rule is what makes runs longer than five reachable at all.

name: Booking the next entrance
effect: Clicking a card on the map sends it to the top of the deck, so it is the first Entrance card of the next show.
why_fun: Lets the map shape the opening hand - a planning tool rather than a power spike.

name: Double Trigger stamp
effect: This card's effects trigger twice.
why_fun: Implemented as StampDoubleTrigger. The workhorse stamp.

name: Revealing stamp
effect: Triggers even while covered by cards above it in its stack.
why_fun: Implemented as StampRevealing. Height stacking is exactly what makes it valuable now.

name: Deck trigger stamp
effect: This card's skill fires while it is still in the draw deck; the trigger animates above the deck slot so it is visible.
why_fun: Global by definition - a card in the deck belongs to no grid.

name: Brass Check stamp
effect: On trigger, mint one Gold card onto the top of the deck.
why_fun: The money-on-trigger seal with a circus name. Global because it writes to the deck.

name: Heavy type
effect: Sinks to the bottom of the deck on every shuffle.
why_fun: Implemented as TypeHeavy.

name: Light type
effect: Rises to the top of the deck on every shuffle - the reliable-draw counterpart to Heavy.
why_fun: Trivially the mirror of TypeHeavy and worth printing for that reason.

name: Elemental types
effect: Earth sits at the bottom, Air at the top, Water moves one position per shuffle, Fire burns itself out of the deck after a set number of shows.
why_fun: Four deck-position behaviours from one visual family; Fire overlaps Glass deliberately.

name: Elemental movement types
effect: Card materials with custom stack behaviour - one always floats to the top of its stack, one always sinks to the bottom of it.
why_fun: Height turns the old deck-position gimmick into a board-position one.

name: Vertical poker hands
effect: Grants columns the poker reading in addition to their run reading, so one column can score twice.
why_fun: A rules card, not a default. It doubles a column's value and is priced for it.

name: Poker Hand of the Four Above
effect: When this card scores, it and the four cards above it in its stack are also scored as a poker hand.
why_fun: The card that most wants height to exist. Dead on a flat board, excellent on a tall one.

name: Every Fifth Card
effect: Every five cards down a column are read as an extra poker hand.
why_fun: Long-column play; only reachable once a grid is stacked above height four.

name: Guaranteed early draw
effect: Cards acquired this show are guaranteed to appear in the first Entrance refills of the next show.
why_fun: Solves the bought-it-never-saw-it problem that makes shops feel bad.

name: Null card
effect: Occupies a cell and highlights on hover, but has no rank or suit and scores nothing.
why_fun: Spatial filler that teaches that position is not points. Also the enemy of the empty-tile blind objective.

name: Hidden trigger
effect: Fires while covered.
why_fun: Shipped as StampRevealing.

name: First hand only
effect: Only the first poker hand scored in a line counts; later ones are ignored.
why_fun: A restriction card, priced as a downside that another card pays you to run.

name: Any card may be placed here
effect: This card accepts any card on top of it regardless of stacking legality.
why_fun: The stacking rules are modifiable by design; this is the simplest possible proof of it.

name: Moving elemental types
effect: Card materials that relocate themselves on the board between placements rather than in the deck.
why_fun: The grid gives this a coordinate to move along at last.

name: Self-upgrading cards
effect: A card that permanently becomes a stronger version of itself once a condition is met during the run.
why_fun: The draft asks whether this differs from an effect at all - it does not, except in presentation, which is the point.

name: Wild pip
effect: Its own pip class that remembers the last pip it copied and behaves as that until it recopies.
why_fun: Tracking the previous pip inside itself is what makes it deterministic across an undo.

name: Chameleon pip
effect: Chooses itself at random from the pips already present in its own row, its own column, or the whole grid.
why_fun: Grid-local by construction - the sample set is the grid. Needs a re-roll rule pinned so undo is stable.

name: Label type
effect: A rule card carrying this type announces its effect on the board even while the rule deck is invisible.
why_fun: Baba-is-you legibility. Without it, hidden rules read as bugs.

name: Linked trigger card
effect: Cue this card to force the card it is stacked with to trigger, whatever that card's own condition is.
why_fun: Turns conditional effects into on-demand ones, which is powerful enough to want a charge limit.

name: Leader cards
effect: Starts the show already on the board or in the Entrance and does not leave when a line scores.
why_fun: The deck's face. Its survival rule is the only thing that makes it structurally different.

name: First Act type
effect: Appears alone in the Entrance before any other card is drawn.
why_fun: Guaranteed opener. Turns one card into a plan.

name: Second Act type
effect: Appears alone once half the deck has been drawn.
why_fun: A midpoint pivot the player can build toward.

name: Final Act type
effect: Appears alone after every other card has been drawn.
why_fun: The closer. Pairs with any end-of-show payout effect.

name: Fireworks suit
effect: A firework rises up its column and banks points into the column directly, scaled by its rank.
why_fun: Shipped as PipSuitFirework. The only suit that scores without a prop interaction.

name: Electric suit
effect: Buffs cards connected to it in an unbroken chain, following adjacency through height as well as across the grid.
why_fun: The suit that most wants the fourth coordinate. Chain length is its rank equivalent.

name: Reroll grants irreversibility
effect: Grants an extra reroll, and for the rest of the show a repeated action never gives the same result twice.
why_fun: A drawback that is also a fantasy - the show cannot be rehearsed.

name: Pandora Box
effect: At show start becomes a random skill; at show end reverts to Pandora Box.
why_fun: Same card with the reset stated, so it never becomes permanently good or permanently dead.

name: Global rule type
effect: A card type whose skill is always in the global spotlight, which is what makes a rule card a rule card.
why_fun: Makes rule cards ordinary cards with one type, so a player can eventually hold one.

name: Homing types
effect: Types that return a card to a named deck when something happens to it.
why_fun: The mechanism behind consumables that come back and blinds that expire.

name: Storyteller
effect: Preserves a portion of this show's score into the next one.
why_fun: The clean way to make a lost show still worth playing out.

name: Entrance mulligan card
effect: Cue to mulligan the Entrance, drawing a fresh set into the empty slots.
why_fun: The card version of the free discard, and the reason the discard need not be free.

name: Rooted cards
effect: A card that resists being moved by effects, its own or anyone's.
why_fun: Rosin in the recommendations. Commitment in exchange for a bonus.

name: Maximum Effort stamp
effect: Doubles this card's points when it scores, then refuses to refresh unless the card sits out the next show entirely.
why_fun: Glass-like risk with a rest mechanic rather than a destruction one.

name: Presentation card
effect: Moving cards in ascending rank order during one turn grants a multiplier.
why_fun: Rewards the order of play rather than the final board, which nothing else does.

name: Chess pawn
effect: Swaps with the card directly above it; from the bottom of a stack it may swap two up; a diagonal move upward captures.
why_fun: The clearest use of height as a chess rank. Capture must swap rather than delete or one piece eats a grid.

name: Chess pieces
effect: Other pieces may move to any cell their chess movement allows, swapping with whatever is there.
why_fun: Swap not capture, so the board's card count is preserved and the piece cannot run away with the show.

name: Chess king
effect: Moves one cell in any direction, never captures, and automatically flees any cell a chess card threatens; enormous points if it is ever captured.
why_fun: An alternate win condition in card form, and the piece that makes the others tactical.

name: Digital type
effect: Cannot be discarded off the board once placed.
why_fun: Anti-removal. Turns a good placement into a permanent one, for better and worse.

name: Clown patience
effect: Each distinct clown card on the board raises maximum patience by one; a full set can spend a move for free.
why_fun: The autochess set bonus, arriving before autochess was named as the source.

name: Rock-paper-scissors suits
effect: A card may only be placed on another if its suit would not lose the matchup; ties resolve by higher rank.
why_fun: An elemental cycle would be the natural flavour. It rewrites placement legality wholesale, so it is a rule card.

name: Negative ranks
effect: Ranks below zero, drawn under an inverting shader; props scoring a negative card subtract points but still add combo.
why_fun: Trades points for multiplier, which is a real decision rather than a strict downside.

name: Dragon suits
effect: Non-standard suits stand in for dragons, which implies more than three ranked suits and more than three dragons.
why_fun: Winds are rejected in the draft as too directional - though the grid now has directions, so they are worth revisiting.

name: Mini hands
effect: A hand is one triplet plus a pair, scaling upward with each extra triplet, rather than a full fourteen-tile hand.
why_fun: Sized to a five-card line. Four triplets and a pair is a whole-grid objective instead.

name: Mahjong discard
effect: Discard any card in a grid that belongs to no meld - a card with no connection to anything in its column.
why_fun: The half-the-fun-is-discarding note, made spatial. Only fires on genuinely dead cards.

name: Mystery Clock
effect: A card with no visible mechanism that nonetheless announces when the next scoring line will complete.
why_fun: Robert-Houdin's glass clock. Information as a card, which the game has too little of.

name: Singing Lesson
effect: Teaches an adjacent card one of its own triggers for the rest of the show.
why_fun: Copying a trigger rather than an effect keeps it from being a strict upgrade.

name: Marvelous Orange Tree
effect: Grows over successive refills - budding, flowering, then fruiting a card into its own column.
why_fun: Robert-Houdin's masterpiece. A card that pays out only if you protect its column for the whole show.

name: Pastrycook of Palais-Royal
effect: Cue to order a card by name from the discard; it is delivered to the Entrance next refill.
why_fun: The automaton that fetched pastries on request. Targeted recursion with a delay.

name: Ethereal Suspension
effect: The card above this one floats - it neither blocks the spotlight nor counts toward stack height.
why_fun: Robert-Houdin's levitation, and a direct counter to the cost of building tall.

name: Endless Bag
effect: Cue to pull a random basic card out of nowhere into the Entrance; never runs out.
why_fun: Infinite chaff is a real resource in a game where placement is the constraint.

name: Eating Contest
effect: Consumes every card in its own stack at show end and scores their combined rank.
why_fun: A stack-capper that pays for building tall and then dismantles it.

name: Dog of 113 Tricks
effect: Each time a distinct effect fires anywhere this show, this card gains a permanent point, up to 113.
why_fun: Rewards a rainbow board over a whole run rather than a whole line.

name: Free Pigs
effect: Gives a random card away to the audience - remove it from the deck and gain two tokens.
why_fun: Barnum's giveaways. A thinning effect that pays instead of costing.

name: Ventriloquist
effect: An adjacent card's skill triggers as though it were this card's, from this card's position.
why_fun: Relocating a trigger is a placement puzzle disguised as a copy effect.

name: Spirit Medium
effect: Cards stack themselves - at each refill, one loose card moves to a legal stack on its own.
why_fun: Auto-moving cards give the board a life of its own, which is unnerving in the right way.

name: Teleport Boxes
effect: Cue to swap the contents of two cells, in any grids.
why_fun: The cross-grid swap. Its whole value comes from there being more than one grid.

name: Levitation
effect: Cue to raise this card one height level, leaving a gap beneath it that the next placement fills.
why_fun: A verb only the fourth coordinate could support.

name: Fake props
effect: A set-piece card that looks like a real card until it is scored, then reveals itself as worthless.
why_fun: The Gaff. Its value is entirely in what an opponent or a blind believes about it.

name: Golden Witch
effect: Spawns Gold cards onto the board through the show; every one of them detonates at show end.
why_fun: Free money with a timer - the board fills with wealth you must spend before it goes off.

name: Narrative cards
effect: Protagonist and villain cards that play out a story across the board, scoring when their scenes complete in order.
why_fun: The quest-shaped effect. Expensive to author, memorable when it lands.

name: Poltergeist
effect: Vanishes an object - removes a card's suit, or repaints it to another suit already on the board.
why_fun: The colour-changing half is the useful half; the vanishing half is the Clown class's job.

name: Crystal Ball
effect: Reveals the next several cards of the deck, as though the answers had been researched in advance.
why_fun: The mitt-camp research gag makes the information feel earned rather than magical.

name: Self-Help Books
effect: Sell copies between shows - gain tokens scaled to how much fame the last show earned.
why_fun: Turns a good show into money without touching the score axis.

name: Snake Charmer
effect: Cards in this column drift one cell toward this card at each refill.
why_fun: Slow gravity, which lets a player set up a formation over several refills.

name: Disappearing Birdcage
effect: Cue to remove this card and a neighbour from the board, returning both to the deck.
why_fun: A reset button for a bad placement, which the one-way grid badly needs.

name: The Vanishing Chair
effect: At the end of each refill this card vanishes and reappears in a different empty cell of its grid.
why_fun: Unpredictable but grid-local, so it never leaves the plan you built it into.

name: Multiplying Balls
effect: When a Balls card scores in this column, add a copy of it to the Entrance.
why_fun: The suit-specific engine card, and the reason to commit a grid to one suit.

name: Expanding Dice
effect: Grows a rank each time a line containing it scores, without limit.
why_fun: Simple, visible growth. The cap is how long you can protect the cell.

name: Nested Boxes
effect: Scores once for each card beneath it in its stack, each time multiplying rather than adding.
why_fun: The card that most rewards a tall stack, and therefore the one that most needs a cost.

name: Self-Playing Instrument
effect: Triggers itself once per refill without being cued.
why_fun: Automation as a card. It makes charges accumulate rather than expire.

name: Floating Head
effect: This card's skill detaches and floats over its grid, staying spotlit wherever it is buried.
why_fun: The theatrical version of the always-active stamp, with the art to justify it.

name: The Band
effect: Scores extra for every distinct class present in its own line.
why_fun: The rainbow reward at line scale rather than board scale.

name: Velocipede
effect: Cue to roll this card along its row until it hits an occupied cell, scoring each empty cell it crosses.
why_fun: Movement that pays for empty space, which nothing else does.

name: Noah's Ark Box
effect: Cue to pour out a flood of animal-class cards into the deck, one per Animal Trainer card already owned.
why_fun: Scales with commitment, which is the right shape for a legendary payoff.

name: Sleight of Hand
effect: Cards moved by effects sometimes land one cell off on purpose, and this card profits when they do.
why_fun: Deliberate imprecision as a mechanic - risky, funny, and only viable with an undo.

name: Bricks from Hats
effect: Cue to convert this card's stamp into a token card placed in an empty cell.
why_fun: Turns equipment back into material, which gives stamps a floor value.

name: Roast to Live Chicken
effect: Cue to bring one card back from the discard as a fresh copy at full rank.
why_fun: Recursion with a transformation attached so it never feels like a plain undo.

name: Blindfold Knife Throw
effect: Cue to name a rank; a knife destroys one random card in the row and scores hugely if it was that rank.
why_fun: Called-shot gambling. The showmanship is in naming it out loud before the throw.

name: The Shuffle
effect: Flips every card in a grid face down, randomises their positions, then reveals the topmost of each stack.
why_fun: Total spatial reset. Terrifying, occasionally exactly what a stuck board needs.

name: Planted Props
effect: Cue to plant a card at a chosen depth in the draw deck, to be produced at exactly the right moment.
why_fun: Prepping hours in advance is the actual trick; the card is just bookkeeping for it.

name: Fake Book Cover
effect: This card displays another card's name and art until it scores.
why_fun: Misdirection as a stamp, and the mechanical partner of the Gaff.

name: Linking Rings
effect: Cards of the Hoops suit in the same row across separate grids count as one continuous line.
why_fun: The long-row rule as a card. Directly rewards playing several grids at once.

name: Straitjacket over Spikes
effect: Starts immobilised over a hazard; frees itself and pays double if its line scores before the show ends.
why_fun: The escape is the payoff. A self-solving problem with a deadline.

name: Niagara Crate
effect: Cue to seal this card and everything above it; the stack is out of play until the next refill, then returns intact.
why_fun: Protects a built stack from a hazard at the cost of a refill's scoring.

name: Tornado of Fire
effect: Cue to set a column alight - every card in it gains Burning, and any card placed there this show gains it too.
why_fun: Turns a column into a commitment. Pairs with anything that pays for Burning.

name: Prince of the Air
effect: Leader whose cards may always move upward through a stack regardless of stacking rules.
why_fun: The Acrobat leader. Height is its whole identity.

name: King of Cards
effect: Leader who may look at and reorder the top of the deck every refill.
why_fun: The Fortune Teller leader. Information rather than power.

name: Lockpicking
effect: Cue to free any one immobilised or restricted card, including one restricted by a blind.
why_fun: The counterplay card blinds need to exist for. Without it, restriction blinds are pure tax.

name: Vanishing Elephant
effect: Cue to remove the entire contents of one cell's stack from play; score for every card removed.
why_fun: The largest single removal in the game, which is exactly what makes it a headline act.

name: Water Torture Cell
effect: Cue to start a three-refill timer; if this card's line has not scored by then, it is destroyed - if it has, it scores triple.
why_fun: A deadline the player sets themselves. Tension without randomness.

name: Walking Through Walls
effect: This card may be placed into an occupied cell, pushing its occupant into the neighbouring grid's matching cell.
why_fun: The clearest cross-grid verb, and it needs the row alignment rule to be legible at all.

name: Rising Cards
effect: Named cards rise out of the deck on their own and arrive in the Entrance at the next refill.
why_fun: The classic effect, and a clean tutor.

name: Disembodied Princess
effect: Only the top half of this card is ever covered - it stays spotlit no matter how tall its stack grows.
why_fun: The illusion and the mechanic are the same picture, which is the ideal for this game.

name: Floating Ball
effect: Cue to send a hoop prop around a Balls card to prove it is unsupported, scoring both.
why_fun: A two-suit combo card that reads as an actual trick.

name: Fake Blood
effect: Appears to destroy an adjacent card; it is only hidden and returns next refill, scoring for the fright.
why_fun: Payoff for the audience believing something went wrong - the risk essay in one card.

name: Indian Rope Trick
effect: Cue to raise a column of cards into a new stack in a single cell, climbing them all upward.
why_fun: Converts spread into height, which is a whole strategy pivot in one action.

name: Tire Trick
effect: Cue to dismantle a stack, hiding its cards; rebuilding the stack later returns them all.
why_fun: Storage that reads as a trick. Pairs with any hazard that targets a stack.

name: Everlasting Flame
effect: Burning applied by this card is not removed by anything, including effects that clear statuses.
why_fun: The counter to status removal, and a reason to keep a Flames build honest.

name: Human Card Index
effect: Cue to name any rank and suit; if that card exists anywhere in your collections, it arrives in the Entrance.
why_fun: The perfect tutor, and the historical act is exactly this - over forty pockets and hundreds of items.

name: Bullfight
effect: A charging prop crosses the row; cards that dodge score, cards that do not are destroyed.
why_fun: A prop that can lose you cards is the risk-reward shape hazards should have.

name: The Sawing
effect: Cue to split a card into two cards of half its rank, same suit, placed in adjacent cells.
why_fun: Rank arithmetic as a tool - fabricate a run on demand.

name: The Expert at the Card Table
effect: Signed by an author nobody can identify; collecting every card bearing the signature unlocks something never explained.
why_fun: The Erdnase cipher. One field on a card, and the community does the rest.

name: Signed Card
effect: When this card leaves the board, the next card created anywhere is this exact card instead.
why_fun: Identity that survives destruction, which no other effect provides.

name: Cups and Balls
effect: Cue to shuffle the positions of three adjacent face-down cards.
why_fun: The oldest trick recorded, and a fine cheap tutorial for the hidden-card rules.

name: Mentalist
effect: Cue to predict a future board state; if it comes true this show, score enormously.
why_fun: Rewards reading the deck and the grid together, which nothing else asks for.

name: Turning Back Time
effect: Cue to undo the last placement without spending an undo, framed as covering an accident.
why_fun: Undo as a card is powerful precisely because the grid commits placements.

name: Funambulist
effect: Crosses its row one cell per refill; if it reaches the far end it scores hugely, and any disturbance drops it.
why_fun: Rope walking as a multi-turn commitment the opponent - or a blind - can interrupt.

name: Slack Rope
effect: This card may be placed between two occupied cells, shifting both outward.
why_fun: Mountebanks walked slack ropes. An insertion verb, which the grid otherwise lacks.

name: Endurance feats
effect: Coal walking, boiling oil, fire swallowing - cards that score for surviving a hazard they were placed into deliberately.
why_fun: The template for any card that wants a blind to exist.

name: Animal novelty
effect: Upright dogs, costumed monkeys, dancing turkeys - low-rarity Animal Trainer cards that score for adjacency to their trainer.
why_fun: The common tier of a class needs cheap adjacency cards like these.

name: Costumed Acrobat
effect: An Acrobat dressed as a beast counts as an Animal card as well as an Acrobat.
why_fun: Class splashing with a historical excuse. The Greasepaint stamp generalises it.

name: Trained Bear
effect: Eats the card directly above it at each refill and gains its rank.
why_fun: Height gives the bear a queue to work through, which paces it naturally.

name: Puppet
effect: Copies the skill of the card to its left for as long as that card remains in play.
why_fun: Puppetry as a copy effect with a visible string - the dependency is the drama.

name: Potion Seller
effect: Cue to sell a card from the deck for tokens; the buyer is never seen again.
why_fun: Saltimbanque economics. A thinning outlet inside a show rather than at a shop.

name: Pickpocket
effect: If this card ends the show without ever scoring, it adds a stolen card to the deck.
why_fun: Rewards not playing a card, which almost nothing else does.

name: Head in the Lion's Mouth
effect: Place adjacent to an Animal card to score triple; if that Animal is ever destroyed, this card is too.
why_fun: Risk stated as a dependency rather than as a dice roll.

name: Military Riders
effect: Scores extra when in a row with two or more cards of its own class, standing in formation.
why_fun: The plainest class-count card, and the tutorial for the autochess rule.

name: Playing Dead
effect: This card is skipped by every destructive effect while it is face down.
why_fun: Protection that costs the card its own scoring while it hides.

name: Automaton and magnet
effect: Cue to pull the nearest card of a chosen suit one cell toward this one.
why_fun: Mechanical attraction as a targeted move, with the magnet as the honest explanation.

name: Long Hair
effect: Hangs from the card above it - counts as part of the stack above rather than below when a line is read.
why_fun: Iron-jaw-by-hair, and a genuinely odd geometry effect.

name: Leaping the Horse
effect: Cue to jump this card back and forth over a neighbour, scoring once per crossing, until it fails.
why_fun: Forty crossings without stopping is the record; the card should tempt the player to push one more.

name: Standing Split
effect: Scores double while it is the only card in its column, and nothing at all once it is not.
why_fun: A card that wants an empty column, which fights every other incentive.

name: Eight-Horse Platform
effect: Scores once per card in its row that is directly supporting it - every card below in the same column counts.
why_fun: Reads the board in two axes at once, which is the grid's signature shape.

name: Catching Oranges
effect: Cue to catch the next prop that would pass this card, scoring it instead of letting it continue.
why_fun: Prop interception - a defensive verb in a system that had only offence.

name: Juggling Variety
effect: Scores once per distinct object type juggled in its column - fruit, bottles, glasses, hoops.
why_fun: A per-column variety reward to sit beside the per-line one.

name: Human Pyramid
effect: Scores for a stack whose ranks strictly decrease upward, once per card in the stack.
why_fun: The formation card the fourth coordinate exists for.

name: Hippodrama
effect: Animal cards may take the leading role - while this is in play, Animal cards count as performers for every class check.
why_fun: Horses treated as actors with billing. A class-wide unlock in one card.

name: The Drunk Spectator
effect: Enters as an ordinary basic card and reveals itself as a performer after it has scored once.
why_fun: The oldest gag in the ring, and a genuinely good surprise the second time you see it.

name: Carried Talent
effect: A talent card stacked on another talent card scores extra, scaling with how many talents are beneath it.
why_fun: Tricks performed atop other performers. The most direct height reward in the notes.

name: Iron Jaw
effect: Supports the entire stack above it - cards above cannot be destroyed or moved while this card holds.
why_fun: Holding weight between the teeth. Anchors a tall stack against hazards.

name: Lion Act
effect: Lions form pedestals, seesaws and bicycles - scores for each distinct formation shape completed in its row.
why_fun: A card that reads shapes, which the diagonal bucket makes possible.

name: Ballet of Elephants
effect: Scores for every Animal card in the grid that shares its row or column with a Dancer card.
why_fun: Fifty ballerinas on fifty elephants. A whole-grid formation payoff.

name: Clown Fire House
effect: When a column burns, clown cards rush in - each Clown in the grid scores and clears one Burning stack.
why_fun: The slapstick skit as counterplay to the game's own fire.

name: Concessions vendors
effect: Peanut, candy, popcorn, balloon and lemonade sellers - common cards that pay tokens when adjacent cards score.
why_fun: The common tier of the Concessions class, and the economy's trickle.

name: Jungle Cats
effect: Panthers and leopards - an Animal card that destroys an adjacent card if no Animal Trainer shares its line.
why_fun: An animal that needs handling, which makes the trainer cards matter.

name: Flaming Cauldron
effect: Cue to dive this card down its whole column, destroying it and scoring for every Burning card it passes.
why_fun: A finisher that spends the card and the column together.

name: Automaton Procession
effect: Mechanical gymnasts and trapezists parade across a row at each refill, triggering each card they pass.
why_fun: A prop that walks the row on a schedule rather than on a score.

name: Niagara Crossing
effect: Cue to walk this card across every grid in one move, scoring for each cell it crosses and falling if any is occupied.
why_fun: A thousand feet of cable, and the longest single move the board allows.

name: Balance Pole
effect: The card this is attached to cannot fail a risk check.
why_fun: The insurance stamp for every gamble card, and the thing a blind should be able to remove.

name: Trapeze Chain
effect: Requires a catcher and a returner - three cards in a row, each triggering the next, scoring more per link.
why_fun: The trapeze act's real structure as a three-card combo.

name: Deliberate Wobble
effect: Cue to fake a mistake - lose points now, and score triple if this card's line completes anyway.
why_fun: The risk essay's thesis card. Performers wobbled on purpose because the gasp was the act.

name: The Web
effect: Dangling ropes - cue to hang a card from the top of its column down to the first empty cell.
why_fun: Aerial ballet as a placement verb, and a use for empty cells low in a column.

name: The Plange
effect: Repeats its own trigger as many times as you dare; each repeat after the first risks an injury stack.
why_fun: Leitzel's one-arm planges, which dislocated her shoulder every performance. Push-your-luck with a real cost.

name: The Low Wire
effect: Only seven feet up but twice as long - moves two cells along its row instead of one, but never changes height.
why_fun: A cheap movement card that trades the fourth coordinate away for reach.

name: Forward Somersault
effect: Moves upward through its stack blind - the destination is not shown until the move resolves.
why_fun: Harder than backwards because the wire cannot be seen. Risk from information, not dice.

name: Human Pyramid on the Wire
effect: Scores for a stack of seven or more, and collapses the whole stack if any card in it is removed.
why_fun: Seven men on one wire. The largest formation payoff with the largest fragility.

name: Wire Bicycle
effect: Carries the card above it along the row as it moves.
why_fun: Transporting a passenger is a distinct verb from moving alone.

name: The Fake Leg
effect: A card wearing this ignores one restriction placed on it by a blind.
why_fun: Wire walking after an amputation. Counterplay stated as equipment.

name: Slipped Straps
effect: Cue to drop this card to the bottom of its stack, scoring for each card it falls past.
why_fun: The faked free fall. A downward verb on a board that otherwise only builds upward.

name: Twenty Tigers
effect: Scores for every Animal card in the grid, and gives this card an injury stack for each one.
why_fun: Wounds flaunted rather than hidden - the scar is the credential.

name: Menagerie
effect: Scores for each distinct Animal card you have ever owned this run.
why_fun: The oddity collection as a long-run reward.

name: Elephants
effect: Only affordable to a wealthy troupe - costs upkeep in tokens every show it stays in the deck.
why_fun: Historically true and mechanically sound: the best cards should cost rent.

name: Lion Pyramid
effect: Scores for a stack made entirely of Animal cards, scaling with its height.
why_fun: The class-specific height formation.

name: Fake Blood Spectacle
effect: Appears to be destroyed when a hazard hits it; it returns at the next refill, and the fright scores.
why_fun: The gorier the better, historically. A survivable destruction is more exciting than a real one.

name: Enraged Beast
effect: Grows more dangerous each refill until an Animal Trainer card is placed in its line, then scores everything it built.
why_fun: Manufactured rage subdued by mastery - a threat that becomes a payoff.

name: Lamb in the Lion Cage
effect: A rank-1 card placed beside an Animal card cannot be destroyed, and both score.
why_fun: Peace as the trick. A defensive card that pays.

name: Peaceful Menagerie
effect: If no card was destroyed this show, every Animal card scores double at the end.
why_fun: The pacifist run condition, and a real strategic fork.

name: Animal Tricks
effect: Globes, tightropes, bicycles and seesaws - common Animal cards that each move one specific way.
why_fun: The common tier of movement, one verb per card.

name: The Animal King
effect: Leader whose Animal cards never gain injury stacks and never turn on their trainer.
why_fun: The Animal Trainer leader.

name: Wrestling the Tiger
effect: Cue to fight an adjacent Animal card - the higher rank wins, the loser is destroyed, the winner scores both ranks.
why_fun: A duel inside a solitaire game, which is a genuinely novel verb.

name: Tarzan
effect: Swings across the row from Animal card to Animal card, scoring at each.
why_fun: Movement that requires a prepared path, which makes the setup the play.

name: Colour-themed clowns
effect: Whiteface clowns keyed to colour - each changes a neighbour's suit to its own.
why_fun: The Clown class's core verb, split across a colour-coded set.

name: Clown as any character
effect: A Clown card may count as any class for one check per refill, since clowns caricature everyone.
why_fun: Class wildcarding with a strong historical justification.

name: Clown Parody
effect: Copies the effect of a card in the same row and scores half of what it scored.
why_fun: Clowns spoofed the rope walkers and the riders. Copying is the class's other verb.

name: Speaking Clown
effect: Announces the next scoring line aloud, revealing what would complete it.
why_fun: Information as banter. Cheap, and it teaches the game.

name: Auguste and Whiteface
effect: The Auguste scores when it fails; the Whiteface scores when it succeeds; together in a row both always score.
why_fun: The defeated clown and the aspiring one, and a two-card engine that always fires.

name: Dan Rice
effect: Leader whose Clown cards may cue twice per refill, talking, singing and dancing through the show.
why_fun: The Clown leader, and the historical superstar clown of American circus.

name: Grock
effect: Copies the last effect that triggered anywhere on the board, whatever it was.
why_fun: The funniest clown in the world, and an infinitely mobile effect to match the face.

name: Transgressive Clown
effect: While in play, one rule card in the rule deck is suspended.
why_fun: Jesters upset the rules of everyday life. The most dangerous card family in the game.

name: The Shortchanging Clown
effect: Pays out tokens now and takes more back at the end of the show.
why_fun: Krusty, the clown who shortchanges the rube. A loan with a face.

name: Cannon Chain
effect: A card fired into a cell containing another cannon is fired again from there, chaining across grids.
why_fun: Explicitly asked for in the newest draft; the cross-grid chain is the payoff.

name: The Great Fall
effect: Cue to drop this card from the top of its stack to the board, scoring for the height it fell.
why_fun: Falling as an act in itself. The mirror of every upward verb.

name: Cannon Woman
effect: Cue to fire this card to the matching cell of an adjacent grid.
why_fun: The clean single-hop cross-grid move, cheaper than the chain.

name: Hair Hang
effect: While hanging beneath another card, this card may still be cued, and scores for the cards above it.
why_fun: Hanging by braided hair while juggling - an act performed from underneath.

name: Strongman Feats
effect: Supports any number of cards above it without the stack becoming unstable.
why_fun: Granite on the torso. The enabler for very tall stacks.

name: Risley Act
effect: Juggles the cards above it - at each refill their order is reversed.
why_fun: Foot juggling of people. Reordering a stack without dismantling it is a rare verb.

name: India-Rubber Man
effect: May be placed in any cell regardless of any placement restriction.
why_fun: Elastic and incomprehensible. The universal answer to restriction blinds.

name: Ladder Violinist
effect: Moves up and down its column each refill, triggering the card it lands on.
why_fun: Two acts at once, which is the joke and the mechanic.

name: Human Corkscrew
effect: Cue to move this card through an occupied cell to the empty cell beyond it.
why_fun: Going through the keyhole. Passing through occupation is a genuinely new movement rule.

name: Fun House Mirror
effect: Distorts adjacent effects - each neighbour's effect fires at double or half strength, chosen at placement.
why_fun: The meta-effect card that the draft itself proposes in the same line.

name: Human Cigarette Factory
effect: Produces one token card per refill using nothing but itself.
why_fun: A self-sufficient generator, priced low because tokens are cheap.

name: Roller Skating
effect: Cue to slide this card one cell along its row into an empty cell.
why_fun: The cheapest movement card in the game, and the one that teaches the verb.

name: Merci
effect: One free illegal move per show, from the solitaire tradition of a single permitted cheat.
why_fun: A named, historical, once-per-show escape hatch. Perfect as a starting-deck card.

name: Accordion combining
effect: Cards three apart in a row, or directly adjacent, may be merged if they match by rank or suit.
why_fun: Accordion solitaire's whole game, as one card. The three-apart rule is the interesting half.

name: Cross-grid bounce
effect: Effects that throw a card into another grid, or swap two cards between grids.
why_fun: The card family the third coordinate exists to serve.

name: Whole-grid mahjong hands
effect: A grid scores if its five rows, or its five columns, contain four triplets and a pair between them.
why_fun: A meld read across a grid rather than a line - the special bucket's natural home.

name: Poker Shuffle
effect: Cue to rearrange any cards already placed, before the grid is full.
why_fun: Explicitly game-breaking - it makes a perfect grid inevitable. Print it once, price it as a legendary.

name: Snap match
effect: When a card is placed matching the rank of the last card placed, both score.
why_fun: Snap, Slapjack and War in one line - reward for consecutive placements matching.

name: Go Fish tutor
effect: Cue to name a rank you already hold; every copy of it in the deck comes to the Entrance.
why_fun: Go Fish's ask, and the requirement to already hold one keeps it honest.

name: Old Maid
effect: A card that cannot be discarded normally and penalises you for holding it at show end; pairs it off to be rid of it.
why_fun: A hot-potato card, which the deck economy currently has no example of.

name: Steal a meld
effect: Cue to add a card to a line that has already scored, rescoring the whole line.
why_fun: 500 Rummy's out-of-turn steal. Rescoring is the strongest verb in the game, so charge for it.

name: Wild stand-ins
effect: A named low rank stands in for any card in a meld.
why_fun: Canasta's twos. Simple, and it makes low ranks worth keeping.

name: Pinochle melds
effect: Marriages of king and queen, the pinochle pairing, and sets of four - melds that care about specific cards, not shapes.
why_fun: A different kind of meld: named cards rather than patterns.

name: Adjacency melds
effect: A marriage that requires the two cards to be exactly adjacent rather than merely in the same line.
why_fun: Adjacency is a stronger constraint than line membership, and the grid makes it readable.

name: Priest and Clown marriage
effect: A themed adjacency meld between two specific classes.
why_fun: Named melds give the class system something to aim at beyond counting.

name: Twenty-one
effect: A line whose ranks total exactly twenty-one scores hugely; over twenty-one scores nothing.
why_fun: Blackjack's bust rule as a line meld. Simple, tense and instantly understood.

name: Tetromino melds
effect: Score for cards forming tetromino shapes, matched by suit or rank.
why_fun: A shape meld that is neither row, column nor diagonal - the special bucket earns its keep.

name: Extreme rank values
effect: Ranks with bespoke point values - an ace worth one or eleven, a ten worth minus ten, a king worth ninety-nine.
why_fun: The 31/99 family. Rank stops being a position and becomes a payout.

name: Loaned cards
effect: A temporary card that lasts a few shows and then leaves, or costs to keep.
why_fun: Game of Life's loans. Rentals give the shop a cheap tier.

name: Sets of three
effect: Any three matching cards in a grid may be cashed for an escalating effect, such as a rank increase.
why_fun: Risk's card sets. Escalation is what makes them worth saving for.

name: Sudoku bonus
effect: A grid whose ranks never repeat in any row or column scores an enormous bonus.
why_fun: A whole-grid objective that fights every other incentive in the game, which is why it pays so much.

name: Hopping cards
effect: Cue to hop this card over an adjacent occupied cell into the empty one beyond.
why_fun: Checkers. The frog card the draft names.

name: Decoder
effect: Sets a secret rank and suit; each placement reports whether it was wrong, right value in the wrong place, or exact.
why_fun: Wordle in a grid. The first line to guess it correctly wins the bonus.

name: Neighbour typing
effect: Scores based on the types of the cards immediately left and right of it.
why_fun: Three Ring Circus's core. The cheapest possible adjacency effect.

name: Cannon into cannon
effect: A card fired into a cell holding another cannon is fired again, chaining launches across grids until it lands somewhere empty.
why_fun: The explicit ask. The chain is the fun, and cross-grid alignment is what makes it readable.

name: Piston
effect: Cue to push the entire row or column of cards one cell along, shunting whatever is at the end into the next grid.
why_fun: Redstone-style pushing. The first effect that moves many cards with one verb.

name: Observer
effect: Fires whenever the card it faces changes - placed on, scored, moved or destroyed.
why_fun: The trigger-on-neighbour-change primitive every chain machine needs.

name: Sticky piston
effect: Pushes a line of cards and pulls them back at the next refill.
why_fun: Reversible movement, which makes a temporary formation possible.

name: Lion
effect: Always counts as a king, whatever its printed rank.
why_fun: A rank override with a face. Makes any card a face card for meld purposes.

name: Shy Clown
effect: May be returned to an empty Entrance slot, but only while the Entrance is attached to the grid it stands in.
why_fun: The first card to make Entrance attachment mechanically visible, which is a genuinely new hook.

name: Sandwich
effect: When this card scores, gain a point for every card between it and the nearest same-suit card further down its stack.
why_fun: Renamed Sliced Bread in the draft. Height is what makes it visible.

name: Selection Sort
effect: Moves up one place in its stack whenever the card above it has a lower rank.
why_fun: A stack that sorts itself over several refills. Deeply satisfying to watch.

name: More Poker
effect: Poker hands score double.
why_fun: The plainest amplifier in the game, and the one every costing model should be calibrated against.

name: Spaceship
effect: May be placed in the void - outside any grid, where it still counts for cross-grid lines.
why_fun: The void is now a real place: the gap between grids. This card lives in it.

name: Self-Placing Card
effect: While in the deck, if a legal empty cell ever exists, this card moves itself there.
why_fun: A card that plays itself, which is unsettling in exactly the right way.

name: Recycler
effect: On score, put two random cards from the discard back into the deck; Exhaust cards do not return.
why_fun: Anti-thinning, which is a real cost in an economy that pays in cards.

name: Egg
effect: When this card scores, it becomes a completely different random card of higher rank.
why_fun: A card that is worth more after you use it, which nothing else does.

name: Champion
effect: Cards of the same rank directly above or below this card in its stack are discarded.
why_fun: Anti-pair, which fights the pair objectives directly. Good tension.

name: All In
effect: On the next score, double the total - and double the fame the next show demands.
why_fun: Borrowing against the future, which is the Hype wager as a card.

name: Deja Vu
effect: Remembers the cell it was placed in; the next time that cell is empty, it returns there from anywhere.
why_fun: A card with a home. The grid gives it a coordinate to remember at last.

name: Rabbit
effect: If this card is grabbed, it bolts to the furthest orthogonal cell instead.
why_fun: Comic, and a genuine obstacle - you have to plan around a card that will not be caught.

name: Trap
effect: Creates an extra empty cell; the next card placed there goes underneath this card instead, and the extra cell disappears.
why_fun: Insertion beneath, which the upward stack makes strange and useful.

name: Goalpost
effect: Enhances a random viable meld type, chosen fresh each show.
why_fun: The trending-meld idea as a card rather than a rule.

name: Distancing
effect: Hovers at the top of its stack without blocking the card beneath it, and cannot be clicked.
why_fun: The Ghost Light stamp's ancestor, and it may count as its own row.

name: Pot of Greed
effect: When this card is alone in its grid's row, discard it and draw two.
why_fun: Conditional on isolation, which the empty-tile objective loves and everything else hates.

name: Rewrite
effect: Remembers the cards beneath it when placed; at show end it replaces that many cards below it with fresh draws.
why_fun: A delayed board rewrite. Expensive to reason about, which is why it is Epic.

name: Paintbrush
effect: Cards this one is placed on take its suit.
why_fun: The Clown class's suit fixer, applied downward through a stack.

name: The One Ring
effect: You always know exactly where this card is; destroy it permanently and win the show outright.
why_fun: An alternate win condition that the destruction family has to work for.

name: No Part of Any Hand
effect: If this card is in no scoring hand at all, it pays a large flat bonus.
why_fun: The anti-meld card, and the empty-chair objective's best friend.

name: Parasite
effect: Attaches to the next card placed on top of it; at show end it replaces its host entirely.
why_fun: Slow theft. The host is visible the whole time, which makes it a decision.

name: Cheering Team
effect: Every scored card sharing this card's suit pays extra.
why_fun: The mono-suit reward that balances the rainbow rewards.

name: Open House
effect: Any card may be stacked on this one, regardless of the stacking rules.
why_fun: Already in the draft's TODO list. The simplest rule-bending card there is.

name: Future Sight
effect: See the next five cards of the deck at all times.
why_fun: Information equal to one whole Entrance ahead. Quiet, and enormously strong.

name: Snake
effect: Consumes lower-ranked cards beneath it in its stack, leaving a temporary body card of the same rank behind.
why_fun: Eats downward and leaves a trail, so the stack keeps its height.

name: Sniper
effect: At each refill, lower the rank of the last card you interacted with by one; at rank one it is discarded.
why_fun: A slow, aimed decline. The targeting rule makes it a real decision.

name: Jenga
effect: Clicking a card that is not on top moves it to the top of the next smallest stack and leaves a gap; clicking a top card does nothing.
why_fun: A whole minigame inside one card, and it only works because stacks have heights to compare.

name: Stowaway
effect: After scoring, moves itself to a free cell if one is open.
why_fun: Survives its own scoring, which is a leader's privilege made common.

name: Combo Memory
effect: During scoring, each card gains temporary points equal to the hand it scored in.
why_fun: Compounds with everything, so it belongs at Rare or higher.

name: Connect Four
effect: Four of a suit in a line, including diagonals, scores as its own meld.
why_fun: A four-length diagonal meld the special bucket can hold.

name: Point Per Trigger
effect: Whenever any card triggers an effect, gain a point.
why_fun: The floor of the effects-as-points economy, and a good common.

name: Tunneler
effect: A single card placed on this one sinks to the bottom of the stack instead.
why_fun: Placement that goes the wrong way, which is disorienting and useful.

name: Noble Family
effect: Each scored face card raises the value of the next scored face card.
why_fun: Escalation within one show, and a reason to hold face cards back.

name: Fishing
effect: Place this card over the deck to open a fishing minigame that pulls a card out of it.
why_fun: The one minigame small enough to survive the deferral of minigames.

name: Turntable
effect: Cue to flip an entire grid vertically.
why_fun: One action, twenty-five cards moved. The largest single rearrangement available.

name: Blackjack Meld
effect: A line totalling exactly twenty-one scores as its own meld.
why_fun: Already deployed as a blind objective; also a fine printed meld.

name: Earth type
effect: Stays at the bottom of the deck.
why_fun: One of the four elemental deck-position types.

name: Air type
effect: Stays at the top of the deck.
why_fun: One of the four elemental deck-position types.

name: Water type
effect: Moves one position down the deck each refill.
why_fun: Remapped from the drop-down version, which is superseded in the catalog.

name: Fire type
effect: Moves one position up the deck each refill.
why_fun: The fourth elemental deck-position type.

name: Money suit
effect: Gold cards act as money at shops and are worth their full trade value.
why_fun: Shipped as the Gold type after the owner's ruling that it works better as a type than a suit.

name: The Joey rank
effect: Jacks become Joeys and count as Clown-class cards.
why_fun: Vetoed in the catalog - a rank that is always eleven is boring, and the Joey should be a clown token with a real effect.

name: The Ringmistress rank
effect: Queens become Ringmistresses and count as Producer-class cards.
why_fun: Vetoed in the catalog; the historical reference can be recycled onto a real card.

name: The Impresario rank
effect: Kings become Impresarios, count as Producer cards and add trade value at shops.
why_fun: Vetoed in the catalog; the reference can be recycled.

name: The Headliner rank
effect: Aces count high or low in runs, decided in your favour at evaluation.
why_fun: Vetoed as a rank rename, but the high-or-low duality is a real spatial decision worth keeping on some card.

name: Harlequin pip
effect: Counts as two suits at once for every comparison, meld and suit effect, firing both props.
why_fun: Vetoed by the owner as boring. The multi-suit stub in the comparator remains, so the mechanism survives the veto.

name: The Gaff
effect: Shows a fixed rank and suit until it scores, then reveals its true random value.
why_fun: Sideshow slang for a faked exhibit. The reveal is the payoff, and the Prepared Town blind is its counter.

name: Half-step rank
effect: Rank five and a half - stacks between five and six but never melds.
why_fun: Owner note - it makes more sense as a hat than as a rank. Same effect, different slot.

name: The Fifteen rank
effect: Also melds with any neighbours whose ranks sum to fifteen with it.
why_fun: Made into a talent rather than a rank, per the owner. It is the demoted cribbage rule given a home.

name: Roman numeral rank
effect: Cosmetic rank skin that melds normally.
why_fun: Accepted. Circus Maximus is where the word circus comes from, so the skin is on-theme.

name: The Blank rank
effect: No rank, no suit - stacks on anything, anything stacks on it, and it scores nothing.
why_fun: Accepted. Free spatial glue that teaches position is not points.

name: Canvas type
effect: The sturdy default for circus-born cards, an upgrade of Paper.
why_fun: Establishes a material progression rather than a single default.

name: Sawdust type
effect: When discarded, leaves a marker on its cell; the next card placed there scores extra.
why_fun: Makes discarding spatial, which the discard-engine essay needs.

name: Rosin type
effect: Sticky - cards placed on it can never be picked up again, but score deeper into the ring bands.
why_fun: The cards-that-resist-being-moved note, given a reason to exist: commitment for reward.

name: Tintype type
effect: On acquisition, permanently copies the pips of the card it was made from.
why_fun: Duplication with lineage. Collectors will chase photographs of photographs.

name: Lithograph type
effect: While in the Entrance rather than in a grid, this card broadcasts its skill globally.
why_fun: A card that wants not to be played, which inverts the whole game's incentive. The Entrance is row -1, so this still works exactly as written.

name: Glass type
effect: Double points when scored; shatters after three scores.
why_fun: Balatro-proven risk and reward, and the timer creates a last-show-for-this-card moment.

name: Wax type
effect: Melts near Flames - loses rank each show it shares a column with a Flames card.
why_fun: Anti-synergy as flavour, and the waxworks really did burn down twice.

name: Ticket Stub type
effect: Spent as currency at shops for a discount; worthless in the Ring.
why_fun: Gives cards-as-currency a small denomination.

name: Flash type
effect: Scores triple, but only the first time it would score in a show.
why_fun: Juggling slang for throwing every prop once. Rewards choreographing when a card enters scoring.

name: Spangle stamp
effect: Adds to the combo when this card is part of any meld.
why_fun: The common-tier workhorse every build wants.

name: Greasepaint stamp
effect: This card counts as a Clown in addition to its own class.
why_fun: The class-splashing enabler every tribal system needs.

name: Top Billing stamp
effect: This card always scores first within its meld.
why_fun: Trigger order is invisible depth; this stamp makes it player-facing.

name: Understudy stamp
effect: If the card above it in the stack is destroyed or consumed, this card copies its skill.
why_fun: Turns destruction effects into setup plays. The flip made above the correct direction.

name: Lloyd's Policy stamp
effect: The first time this card would be destroyed or debuffed, prevent it.
why_fun: Insurance against the game's own debuff system, and performers really did insure body parts.

name: Ghost Light stamp
effect: Does not block the spotlight of cards beneath it.
why_fun: The counterweight the ring-depth tension needs - build tall without killing your engines.

name: The Encore stamp
effect: If this card's skill triggered this show, it has a chance to trigger once more at show end.
why_fun: The end-of-show lottery tick.

name: Contract Ink stamp
effect: Pays extra per show it is played, and leaves the deck if benched two shows running.
why_fun: Anti-autopilot pressure, and performers really did jump between rival shows.

name: Wall of Death
effect: Adjacent columns gain a multiplier, and cards in them take an Exhaust debuff each show.
why_fun: An aura with a cost, where placement decides who pays it.

name: The Seance Buster
effect: Reveals every Gaff, Humbug and disguised card on the board and scores per fake revealed.
why_fun: Counterplay that makes fakes a real subgame. Houdini against the mediums is history's best rivalry.

name: The Erdnase Cipher
effect: An author signature that appears on random cards across many runs; collecting and scoring all of them unlocks something never explained.
why_fun: Erdnase wrote card handling's bible in 1902 and his identity is still unknown. Never explain it.

name: The Forty-Two Foot Ring
effect: A secret meld that fires when a grid's row and column scores total exactly forty-two.
why_fun: Astley's ring is forty-two feet because of horse physics. Hide the number everywhere.

name: The Sword Swallower meld
effect: A column that is one perfect descending run from top to bottom.
why_fun: A secret meld the player can stumble into and then chase deliberately.

name: The Joey leader
effect: Leader granting one free Slapstick - a swap of two adjacent ranks - every refill.
why_fun: Joseph Grimaldi, Regency London's superstar clown and the reason clowns are still called Joeys.

name: Beni Hasan jugglers
effect: The oldest depiction of juggling, from an Egyptian tomb around 1994 BCE - the origin card for the Balls suit.
why_fun: The suit already ships; this is its provenance.

name: Dedi
effect: The magician of the Westcar Papyrus, who reattached severed heads - a card that restores a destroyed card to the board intact.
why_fun: Restoration is rarer than destruction and should stay that way.

name: Acetabularii
effect: Rome's cups-and-balls performers - shuffle the positions of face-down cards.
why_fun: The oldest continuously performed trick on Earth.

name: Bull-leaping
effect: Minoan acrobats vaulting a charging bull - move over a hazard card and score for surviving it.
why_fun: Around 1500 BCE, and the earliest recorded danger act.

name: Funambulus
effect: The Latin for rope-walker, still the technical term - the wire-crossing card's proper name.
why_fun: Petauristarii were the acrobats; funambulus the rope-walker.

name: Sword Swallowing origin
effect: Ascetic demonstrations of bodily control from India, by tradition around 2000 BCE - swallow the card above you.
why_fun: The provenance for the Sword Swallower card.

name: Jongleurs
effect: Itinerant do-everything performers - a card that counts as three different classes at once but scores less in each.
why_fun: The medieval generalist, and the argument that variety predates specialisation.

name: The Fool's License
effect: The one performer permitted to mock the king - while in play, one restriction from the blind is ignored.
why_fun: Truth wrapped in folly, and the cleanest counterplay card in the file.

name: The Marotte
effect: The jester's sceptre topped with a miniature of his own head - this card carries a miniature copy of its own skill that triggers separately.
why_fun: A stamp that duplicates rather than modifies.

name: Mr Punch
effect: The hook-nosed Neapolitan puppet who became England's Punch - destroys an adjacent card and scores, every time, without consequence.
why_fun: That is the way to do it. A card that gets away with it is genuinely funny.

name: Till Eulenspiegel
effect: The prankster who takes every instruction maliciously literally - this card fulfils the letter of a blind's objective in the least useful way and still scores.
why_fun: A card built on rules-lawyering, which the rule deck makes possible.

name: Mountebanks
effect: Renaissance stage-medicine sellers - cue to sell a card whose effect is not what was advertised.
why_fun: The ancestors of the medicine show, and of the Potion Seller card.

name: The Conjurer
effect: Bosch's painting of a cups-and-balls show where an accomplice picks the absorbed spectator's pocket - this card steals while an adjacent card holds attention.
why_fun: A two-card combo painted in 1502.

name: The Discoverie of Witchcraft
effect: Reginald Scot exposed conjuring methods in 1584 to save accused witches from execution - reveal every hidden card on the board.
why_fun: Exposure as mercy. Better history than any invented flavour.

name: The Courier of St Petersburg
effect: Ducrow's signature act, standing astride multiple horses at once - this card occupies two adjacent cells and scores in both lines.
why_fun: A card that straddles two columns, which is a genuinely new geometry.

name: Pablo Fanque
effect: The first Black British circus proprietor, whose 1843 poster the Beatles lifted verbatim for Mr Kite.
why_fun: A leader whose poster is his signature - the billing itself is the effect.

name: Lord George Sanger
effect: The showman who awarded himself a peerage in answer to Buffalo Bill's Honourable - this card promotes itself a rarity tier and charges accordingly.
why_fun: Self-conferred status as a mechanic.

name: Carl Hagenbeck
effect: Revolutionised animal acts with reward-based gentling instead of fear, and invented the cageless enclosure - a leader whose Animal cards never need a trainer adjacent.
why_fun: The humane alternative, and historically the more successful one.

name: The Seven-Person Pyramid
effect: The Wallendas' seven-person pyramid, and its 1962 collapse - a stack of seven that scores enormously and falls entirely if any card is removed.
why_fun: The most famous formation in circus history, with its failure mode included.

name: Con Colleano
effect: The Wizard of the Wire, first to land a feet-to-feet forward somersault on the tightwire.
why_fun: The forward somersault card's historical anchor.

name: Bird Millman
effect: The Ziegfeld-era wire dancer - a Dancer-class card that moves along a row while scoring formations.
why_fun: Naming source for the wire-dancer card.

name: Gargantua
effect: Ringling's acid-scarred gorilla, whose forced grin was billed as ferocity - a card whose printed threat is entirely marketing and whose real effect is gentle.
why_fun: Marketing genius and animal cruelty in the same act. Handle the framing carefully.

name: Chang and Eng Bunker
effect: The original conjoined twins, who toured on their own terms and became successful businessmen - two cards that must be placed adjacent and score as one.
why_fun: They controlled their own billing, which is the part worth telling.

name: Anna Swan and Martin Bates
effect: The giantess and the giant who married - two cards that score for their combined height in a stack.
why_fun: Nearly fifteen feet together.

name: Johnny Eck
effect: The Amazing Half-Boy - performer, artist and illusion-builder with his twin. A card that occupies only the upper half of a cell, leaving room beneath.
why_fun: Half a cell is a new placement geometry.

name: Prince Randian
effect: The Human Torso, who rolled and lit cigarettes with his lips across forty-five years - a card that produces a token every refill using nothing.
why_fun: The Human Cigarette Factory's real name.

name: Violet and Daisy Hilton
effect: Conjoined-twin vaudeville stars with saxophone and jazz - this card doubles an adjacent card's trigger when both score together.
why_fun: Twin harmony as a mechanic.

name: Betty Broadbent
effect: The tattooed lady - five hundred and sixty-five tattoos across forty years. The Illustrated card holds several stamps at once.
why_fun: The multi-stamp card, with a real body behind it.

name: The Living Skeleton and the Fat Lady
effect: Battersby and Perkins, the sideshow's beloved odd couple - two cards whose ranks average when they are adjacent.
