why_fun: Averaging is a verb nothing else in the game has.

name: Zip the Pinhead
effect: Sixty years performing a mystery Barnum never explained - a card whose effect is never written on it and never told.
why_fun: The purest secret card the game could print.

name: The Durov Dynasty
effect: Animal-trainer clowns famed for kindness-based training and political satire.
why_fun: A leader who is both Clown and Animal Trainer, which no other card is.

name: Oleg Popov
effect: The Sunshine Clown, gentle and wordless, beloved across the Cold War divide - a card that removes one negative status from every card in its grid.
why_fun: Kindness as a mechanic, which the game has too little of.

name: Yuri Nikulin
effect: The clown so beloved he became a film star and ran the Moscow circus.
why_fun: A Clown leader whose signature is fame rather than mischief.

name: Karandash
effect: The Pencil, the USSR's defining clown, with his dog Klyaksa - the Inkblot. A card that draws a permanent mark on a cell.
why_fun: A clown who leaves marks on the board is a good fit for the cell-modifier family.

name: Dzhigitovka
effect: Cossack trick riding - hanging off the saddle at full gallop to pick objects off the ground. This card collects a card from a cell it passes without stopping.
why_fun: Movement plus collection in one verb.

name: Hoop Diving and Chair Stacking
effect: Precision diving through towers of hoops, and chairs balanced to the ceiling - a card that scores for the height of the stack it dives through.
why_fun: The Chinese source for both the hoop suit and the height coordinate.

name: Lion Dance
effect: Two performers inside one lion, pole-jumping in the southern style - two cards that move as one unit.
why_fun: Paired movement, which is distinct from paired scoring.

name: Sun Wukong
effect: The Monkey King's seventy-two transformations - a card that becomes any other card on the board, once per refill.
why_fun: The acrobat role of Chinese opera, and the best copy card available.

name: You Meng
effect: The jester of Chu, who impersonated a dead minister so movingly the king restored his family's fortune - a card that copies a card removed from play.
why_fun: Impersonation as advocacy, around 600 BCE.

name: Hard Qigong
effect: Iron-head and spear-against-throat demonstrations - a card that cannot be destroyed while it is spotlit.
why_fun: Conditioning as armour.

name: Money-Suited Cards
effect: Early Chinese decks used currency as suits - coins, strings of coins, myriads.
why_fun: The historical precedent for the Gold suit, and the reason it works.

name: Daikagura
effect: Lion dance and juggling as a Shinto blessing - juggling as literal purification. This card clears every negative status from the line it scores in.
why_fun: Sacred juggling, which recasts the Balls suit entirely.

name: Kyokugoma
effect: Edo virtuoso top-spinning; Matsui Gensui toured the West in the 1860s. A spinning card that keeps its effect alive for several refills.
why_fun: A timed effect with a visible spin-down.

name: Shokyokusai Tenkatsu
effect: The superstar female magician of Meiji and Taisho Japan, who ran her own troupe.
why_fun: The Magician leader.

name: Karakuri Ningyo
effect: Edo clockwork automata - the tea-serving doll that trundles to a guest and waits. A card type that moves itself to a target and stops.
why_fun: Self-moving cards with a destination, not a direction.

name: Bunraku
effect: Three visible operators animating one puppet, with total audience buy-in - three cards that jointly control a fourth.
why_fun: A four-card formation that nothing else in the game resembles.

name: Sarumawashi
effect: Street monkey-trainer performances, a thousand years old - a token that climbs the stack and returns.
why_fun: A token with a route rather than a target.

name: Mallakhamb
effect: The wrestler's pole - gymnastics performed wrapped around a wooden pole, which makes the column itself the apparatus.
why_fun: The clearest historical argument that a column is a piece of equipment.

name: The Great Indian Rope Trick
effect: The most famous trick that probably never existed, largely a newspaper invention of 1890 - a card whose effect is only described, never seen.
why_fun: A legendary whose whole point is that nobody can prove it happened.

name: The Basket Trick
effect: A performer vanishes into a basket run through with swords and reappears unharmed in the crowd - a card removed from play that returns to a different cell.
why_fun: Removal and return, with the swords as the reason it reads as risk.

name: The Mango Seed
effect: A seed grows into a fruiting tree in minutes under a cloth - a rank-one card that grows while covered.
why_fun: An anti-spotlight card that wants to be buried.

name: P C Sorcar
effect: India's great showman-magician, whose 1956 BBC sawing ran past the broadcast cutoff and left a nation believing it had watched a death.
why_fun: A card whose effect resolves one refill later than expected, on purpose.

name: Snake Charming
effect: The been and the swaying cobra, which responds to motion rather than to music - a card that pulls another along its column by moving.
why_fun: The correction is the good detail: it follows the instrument, not the tune.

name: Vidushaka
effect: The Sanskrit-drama jester and Kerala's temple jester-narrator, licensed to mock anyone present.
why_fun: Another entry in the fool's-licence family, from a different tradition.

name: Bed of Nails
effect: Ascetic endurance turned spectacle - fire walking and beds of nails recur across Greece, Fiji and India.
why_fun: A card that takes weight without breaking, which the tall-stack family needs.

name: Uran Nugaralt
effect: Mongolian contortion, a national art with the world's most celebrated lineage - a card that fits into any cell shape a blind imposes.
why_fun: The India-Rubber Man's better-sourced sibling.

name: Rifa'i Demonstrations
effect: Skewers and blades passed through flesh without visible harm - faith as proof.
why_fun: A protection card whose flavour is conviction rather than equipment.

name: Moroccan Acrobats
effect: The Tazeroualt tumbling brotherhood, whose human pyramids and banquine throws toured the world.
why_fun: The pyramid formation with a specific lineage.

name: The Gali-Gali Men
effect: Egyptian street cups-and-balls masters famed for producing live baby chicks - a card that creates a token wherever it moves.
why_fun: Production rather than transformation.

name: Karagoz and Hacivat
effect: The Turkish shadow-play duo - the earthy trickster and the pompous scholar, bickering for five centuries. Two cards that score more when adjacent and argue when apart.
why_fun: A pair whose whole value is the pairing.

name: Zurkhaneh
effect: The House of Strength - ritual club-swinging and drumming in an ancient athletic brotherhood.
why_fun: The Strongman family, sourced to a living tradition.

name: Darvoz Rope-Walkers
effect: Central Asian high-rope dynasties performing at festivals for centuries.
why_fun: A wire card that crosses between grids rather than within one.

name: Griots
effect: West African hereditary praise-singers and living archives - a card that remembers everything the run has done and scores for it.
why_fun: Memory as a mechanic, and the only card that reads the whole run's history.

name: Moko Jumbies
effect: Carnival stilt-walking guardians who see over evil - a card that sees and protects the whole column beneath it.
why_fun: Guardianship with a height requirement.

name: Danza de los Voladores
effect: Four flyers descend a thirty-metre pole on ropes, circling thirteen times each - a card that descends its stack scoring once per level.
why_fun: Thirteen circles times four is the solar year, which is a meld waiting to be printed.

name: Aztec Antipodism
effect: Foot-jugglers spinning logs, documented in 1528 and taken to the court of Charles V - a card that supports and spins the card above it.
why_fun: The Risley act's older name and better provenance.

name: Rodeo Clown
effect: The clown whose real job is drawing the bull away from fallen riders - this card redirects a hazard onto itself.
why_fun: The protection family's clearest single card.

name: Congress of Rough Riders
effect: Buffalo Bill's touring mega-show mixed cowboys, Cossacks and cavalry from everywhere - a card that scores for the number of distinct classes on the whole board.
why_fun: The rainbow reward at board scale, and the historical original of the variety show.

name: The Rattlesnake King
effect: Clark Stanley's snake oil, which contained no snake oil - a card sold at a shop whose printed effect is not its real one.
why_fun: The medicine show, and the origin of a phrase.

name: Wing Walkers
effect: Barnstormers and wing-walkers of the 1920s - a card that transfers between grids while both are in motion.
why_fun: A mid-flight transfer, which is the most dangerous move in the file and should score like it.

name: Annie Edson Taylor
effect: A sixty-three-year-old teacher, first over Niagara in a barrel, who saw almost no money from it.
why_fun: A card that survives an enormous risk and is paid almost nothing - which is worth printing honestly.

name: The Great Farini
effect: The Niagara rope-crosser who became an impresario and designed the human-cannonball apparatus.
why_fun: A leader who builds the props other cards use.

name: Steve Brodie
effect: Claimed, probably falsely, to have jumped off the Brooklyn Bridge, and became famous anyway - a card that scores for a feat it never performs, unless it is inspected.
why_fun: Fame from an unverified claim, which is the Gaff family's purest case.

name: High-Diving Horses
effect: The Steel Pier act, whose rider Sonora Webster continued after being blinded.
why_fun: An Animal card that dives the full height of its stack.

name: Capoeira
effect: A martial art disguised as dance by enslaved Afro-Brazilians - the roda circle, the berimbau, and a fight the authorities could not see.
why_fun: The ban-workaround family's founding card. Treat the history with weight.

name: Bumba Meu Boi
effect: The folk pageant beneath Parintins - the prize ox is killed and resurrected amid celebration.
why_fun: A card that must die to pay out, and comes back.

name: Tango
effect: Born in dockside courtyards and brothels, then conquered Paris - the embrace, the lead and the follow.
why_fun: Two cards that move as a pair, one leading and one following.

name: Frevo
effect: Carnival music so frenetic that dancers invented the passo - acrobatics steadied by a tiny umbrella.
why_fun: A prop that permits a move otherwise illegal. The umbrella is the enabler.

name: May Wirth
effect: The Australian equestrienne called the greatest ever, and the only performer landing a backward-backward somersault between horses.
why_fun: A movement card whose whole claim is that only one person ever did it.

name: Haka and Kapa Haka
effect: The challenge dance, performed at welcomes, funerals and tests, and the competitive group form.
why_fun: A whole-line card performed in unison. Treat the reference respectfully.

name: Siva Afi
effect: The Samoan fire-knife dance - the ailao war dance armed with a machete wrapped in burning towels.
why_fun: Knives and Flames in one card, which is the dual-suit idea with a real source.

name: Naghol
effect: Pentecost Island land diving - men dive from thirty-metre towers with vines tied to their ankles, calculated to stop just short.
why_fun: The Vine stamp: survive a fall from any height, exactly once.

name: Jultagi
effect: Korean tightrope walking with stand-up comedy - the walker jokes mid-wire and works the crowd.
why_fun: An Acrobat card that is also a Clown card, and better for it.

name: Talchum
effect: Korean masked satire mocking aristocrats and monks, with licence to insult the powerful.
why_fun: Another fool's-licence card, from a tradition where the licence was explicit.

name: Sangmo
effect: Pungmul drummers spinning long ribbons from swivel-hats while drumming and leaping.
why_fun: A prop that traces a path over several cells while its card stays put.

name: Reog Ponorogo
effect: A dancer carries a fifty-kilogram lion-peacock mask gripped in his teeth.
why_fun: The Iron Jaw card with the heaviest documented load.

name: Kuda Lumping
effect: Javanese trance horse-dancers on woven bamboo horses, who in trance eat glass.
why_fun: A status that grants immunity and costs control.

name: Kecak
effect: The monkey chant - a hundred bare-chested men as a single interlocking voice-orchestra, devised in the 1930s.
why_fun: A line where every card contributes one interlocking part and none scores alone.

name: Water Puppetry
effect: Vietnamese puppets dance on a pond while the puppeteers stand waist-deep behind a screen.
why_fun: Hidden but active - the anti-spotlight family with the prettiest staging.

name: Likay
effect: Glitter-drenched improvised Thai folk theatre, where audiences pin money on performers mid-scene.
why_fun: Tips arriving during the act rather than after it.

name: Wau Bulan
effect: Malaysian giant moon-kites with hummers that sing in the wind.
why_fun: A prop that stays aloft over a column and hums until it lands.

name: Steelpan
effect: When drums were banned, Trinidadians hammered melody out of oil barrels and invented an instrument.
why_fun: The ban-workaround family's best outcome - a restriction that produces something new.

name: Dubplate
effect: Jamaican sound systems battle for crowds, and the ammunition is the dubplate - an exclusive cut nobody else has.
why_fun: A card that exists in one copy in one run, and is worth more for it.

name: Rara
effect: Haitian Lenten street processions with bamboo vaksin trumpets - bands walk for miles gathering crowds.
why_fun: A card that collects other cards as it travels a row.

name: Castells
effect: Catalan human towers up to ten levels, crowned by the enxaneta - a small child who climbs to the very top and raises a hand.
why_fun: The crown rule is the mechanic: the smallest card must top the tower for it to count.

name: Las Fallas
effect: Valencian neighbourhoods spend a year building enormous satirical sculptures and then burn every one, except a single pardoned ninot.
why_fun: Build-to-burn, with one survivor chosen by vote. Investment that pays out on destruction.

name: Recortadores
effect: Spanish bull-leaping - dodging and vaulting the bull with no harm done to it.
why_fun: The Minoan act, still performed, and the humane version of the Bullfight card.

name: The Costaleros
effect: Monumental Holy Week floats carried through cities by hidden bearers sweating underneath.
why_fun: Covered cards add their rank to the card they carry - the anti-spotlight family's best mechanic.

name: Fado
effect: Portuguese song as performed longing - mourning what is gone, as public art.
why_fun: A card that scores for what the run has lost rather than for what it holds.

name: Czech Marionettes
effect: Under occupation, puppets kept the Czech language and its satire alive when people could not speak.
why_fun: The ban-workaround family, again, and its most literal case.

name: Hopak
effect: The Ukrainian squat-kick acrobatic dance - explosive, competitive and showy.
why_fun: A burst move that launches a card upward one level.

name: The Bauta
effect: The Venetian mask that let all classes mingle anonymously - nobles gambled beside servants.
why_fun: A stamp that hides a card's rarity, which several blinds care about.

name: Gumboot Dance
effect: South African miners forbidden to speak invented a slap-and-stamp boot code.
why_fun: A card that communicates with others in its line while an effect silences them.

name: Azmari
effect: Ethiopian wandering minstrels famed for wax and gold - lyrics with a surface meaning and a hidden one.
why_fun: A card whose printed text says one thing and whose real effect is the other.

name: Sogo Bo
effect: Malian puppet-masquerade festivals of animal spirits on the Niger - whole ecosystems danced.
why_fun: A card that spawns a set of Animal tokens that interact with each other.

name: Ajaraaq
effect: Inuit string figures - story-patterns woven between the hands.
why_fun: A card that scores for the shape the board makes rather than for its values.

name: Flyer and Catcher
effect: The trapeze duet - one throws, one catches, and trust is the art form.
why_fun: Two cards where one launches and the other must be in position to receive.

name: Iron Jaw and Hair Hang
effect: Aerialists suspended by their teeth, or by braided hair in the Chinese tradition.
why_fun: Two support cards from one act, differing in what they can carry.

name: The Aerial Family
effect: Cloud swing, corde lisse, Spanish web and silks - the rope-and-fabric family.
why_fun: Four movement cards distinguished by how far and how controllably they descend.

name: Philippe Petit
effect: The illegal 1974 wire-walk between the Twin Towers, prepared in secret for years.
why_fun: A cross-grid walk that must be set up over several refills before it can be taken.

name: Karl Wallenda
effect: The patriarch who walked until seventy-three and died on the wire - being on the wire is life, the rest is waiting.
why_fun: A leader who cannot stop performing, and is penalised for a refill spent idle.

name: Maria Spelterini
effect: Crossed Niagara on a wire in 1876 with peach baskets strapped to her feet.
why_fun: A movement card with a self-imposed handicap that multiplies the payout.

name: Enrico Rastelli
effect: The god of jugglers, who trained obsessively and died at thirty-four, and whose records are still argued about.
why_fun: The Balls-suit leader, whose signature is sheer count.

name: Paul Cinquevalli
effect: The Victorian greatest juggler - billiard balls and everyday objects handled with elegance.
why_fun: A card that treats any adjacent card as a prop it can juggle.

name: Gentleman Jugglers
effect: Kara and the immaculate evening-dress school - hats, canes and cigars, the everyday made impossible.
why_fun: Props drawn from ordinary cards rather than from the suit.

name: W C Fields
effect: The vaudeville tramp juggler whose fake mistakes got bigger laughs than his tricks.
why_fun: The Deliberate Wobble card's American source.

name: Kris Kremo
effect: Cigar-box virtuosity - three boxes and decades of variations.
why_fun: Rearrange three cards in a stack in a single action.

name: The Manipulation Family
effect: Devil sticks, poi and staff - the object-manipulation family across cultures, poi from Maori tradition.
why_fun: Three common prop cards, with the poi entry carrying its provenance.

name: Louis Cyr's Backlift
effect: The Canadian who back-lifted a platform of eighteen men - this card scores for every card resting above it.
why_fun: The purest anti-spotlight card: it wants to be buried under as much as possible.

name: Katie Sandwina
effect: Bent iron bars and lifted her husband overhead nightly for decades - carries one card without it counting as covering.
why_fun: Support that does not block the spotlight.

name: The Mighty Atom
effect: A five-foot-four strongman who bit through nails, restrained aircraft and broke chains with his chest.
why_fun: A low-rank card that behaves as a high one for every strength check.

name: Hadji Ali
effect: The regurgitation act - swallowed water and kerosene and fountained them separately, extinguishing and reigniting a fire.
why_fun: A card that stores two effects and releases them in either order.

name: The Mirror Shot
effect: Sharpshooters firing over the shoulder using a mirror, as Oakley and Topperwein did.
why_fun: A card that targets by reflection - the cell mirrored across the grid's centre.

name: Buried Alive reference
effect: The fakir tradition and Houdini's last stunts - interment endurance, which Houdini nearly died failing.
why_fun: The Buried Alive card's source, with the failure included.

name: The Escape Chain
effect: The Water Torture Cell - upside down, ankles locked, and a series of restraints that must be undone in order.
why_fun: Several restrictions removed one per refill, which is a quest inside one card.

name: Fire Acts
effect: Fire eating, fire breathing and full-body burns - vaporised-fuel plumes and stunt burns, the least forgiving discipline there is.
why_fun: The Flames suit's most dangerous tier.

name: Edith Clifford
effect: Swallowed a bayonet mounted on a rifle butt while the band played.
why_fun: The Sword Swallower card's specific and astonishing source.

name: The Globe of Death
effect: Motorcyclists riding vertical walls and mesh spheres - a card that circles its column continuously without leaving it.
why_fun: Centrifugal movement, which is a loop rather than a path.

name: Zazel
effect: The first human cannonball, 1877, and the Zacchini family who made it a dynasty with compressed air and faked smoke.
why_fun: The Human Cannonball card's source, including the fact that the explosion was theatre.

name: Human Blockhead
effect: Melvin Burkhart hammering a nail into his nasal cavity, with comedy timing rather than gore.
why_fun: A cheap card whose delivery is the whole act.

name: Grock reference
effect: The Swiss king of clowns, whose musical virtuosity was perpetually defeated by furniture.
why_fun: Provenance for the Grock card.

name: Isaac Fawkes
effect: The 1720s fairground conjurer who died rich on the egg bag and the blooming apple tree.
why_fun: A card that produces cards indefinitely and made its owner wealthy - the economy engine with a face.

name: Matthew Buchinger
effect: Born without hands or legs; a virtuoso magician, marksman and micrographic calligrapher who hid psalms inside the curls of his own portrait.
why_fun: A card with a secret written into its art, discoverable only by looking closely.

name: Robert-Houdin
effect: The watchmaker who invented modern magic - evening dress instead of robes, mechanical marvels, and the whole grammar of the stage.
why_fun: The Magician leader, and the clockwork theme's origin.

name: The Great Wizard of the North
effect: John Henry Anderson, a pioneer of publicity, ruined three times by theatre fires and rebuilding each time.
why_fun: A card that returns stronger after each run it loses.

name: Adelaide Herrmann
effect: The great Herrmann died mid-tour and Adelaide took over the show, performing for decades after.
why_fun: A leader who inherits - when your leader is lost, this one takes the run over.

name: Harry Blackstone Sr
effect: The vanishing birdcage and the floating lightbulb - and the night he calmly evacuated a burning theatre by pretending it was part of the act.
why_fun: A card that turns a disaster into a performance and scores for it.

name: Cardini
effect: Endless fans of cards materialising at the fingertips of a bemused, tipsy gentleman.
why_fun: A card that produces another card every refill and appears surprised each time.

name: The Zancigs
effect: Two Minds with but a Single Thought - a husband-and-wife second-sight code act.
why_fun: Two cards in different grids that share information and score together.

name: Arthur Lloyd
effect: The Human Card Index, who could produce any requested card or document from his forty pockets.
why_fun: The perfect tutor, already drafted from the game notes and confirmed here.

name: P T Selbit
effect: Invented sawing a woman in half in 1921, and walking through a wall.
why_fun: Provenance for two cards the draft already names.

name: Channing Pollock
effect: The elegant dove worker who made bird production high art.
why_fun: A card that produces an Animal token each time it scores.

name: Vanishing the Statue
effect: Copperfield vanished the Statue of Liberty in 1983 - the largest illusion ever staged.
why_fun: Remove an entire grid from view for one refill, and bring it back untouched.

name: Ricky Jay
effect: Card-throwing lethality, fifty-two assistants, and the scholarship of forgotten performers.
why_fun: A card thrown as a weapon along a row, which is the knife suit with a deck instead.

name: The Fox Sisters
effect: Spiritualism was born in 1848 from two girls cracking their toe joints, and Margaret confessed forty years later.
why_fun: A card whose enormous effect is revealed as a trick, and stops working once exposed.

name: Spirit Photography
effect: Mumler's double-exposure ghosts, and cheesecloth ectoplasm - a card that shows a faint copy of a card removed from play.
why_fun: Fakery that produces something genuinely useful, which is the Gaff family's best form.

name: Waxworks
effect: Madame Tussaud's death-mask realism as touring spectacle, and the Chamber of Horrors.
why_fun: The Wax type, sourced - it melts near Flames because wax does.

name: Zoltar
effect: Coin-op prophecy cabinets of the penny arcade.
why_fun: A machine that sells you one prediction per show.

name: The Ace of Spades
effect: English decks paid duty through an ornate official ace, and forging it was a hanging offence.
why_fun: A stamp that proves a card is legitimate, and a Forged Ace that pretends.

name: The Joker
effect: Born as Euchre's Best Bower, the deck's newest card, later adopted by magicians and printers as a signature.
why_fun: The wild rank, with its actual history rather than its assumed one.

name: George Devol
effect: The Mississippi riverboat sharp of Forty Years a Gambler, who head-butted opponents like a battering ram.
why_fun: A Gambler leader whose signature is that losses cost less.

name: Poker Alice
effect: The frontier's famous female dealers - Poker Alice and Madame Moustache.
why_fun: A Gambler leader for a gambling-focused deck.

name: Escape Map Decks
effect: The US Playing Card Company hid escape maps inside cards sent to prisoner-of-war camps in the Second World War.
why_fun: A card that reveals a hidden route on the map when peeled apart, once.

name: The Mitt Camp
effect: Palmistry, tasseography and phrenology - the midway's pseudo-sciences.
why_fun: Fortune Teller class flavour, with the honest note that none of it worked.

name: The Brass Ring
effect: Carousel riders grabbed at a brass ring for a free ride, an idea born from cavalry lance training.
why_fun: Reach out from a moving card to claim a bonus - the origin of grabbing the brass ring.

name: The 24-Hour Man
effect: The advance agent marking tomorrow's route on poles and fences.
why_fun: Reveals the next node's blind a show early.

name: The Greek Chorus
effect: The ensemble that watches, comments and warns - inside the story and outside it.
why_fun: A card that scores for what other cards do without ever acting itself.

name: Thalia and Melpomene
effect: The comedy and tragedy masks, worn as one symbol.
why_fun: A card with two effects, one for a winning board and one for a losing one.

name: The Prima Donna
effect: The diva whose demands reorganise the whole company - the strongest card scores double and every other card scores less.
why_fun: A card that is worth building around and painful to build around.

name: The Encore Exit
effect: Leave the stage, be called back, return bigger - voluntarily discard this card to have it return next refill at double value.
why_fun: The encore as a mechanic rather than as a chance.

name: He's Behind You
effect: British panto's sacred contract - the crowd screams warnings the performer pretends not to hear.
why_fun: A card that is warned about an incoming hazard and may choose to ignore it.

name: The Heel Turn
effect: The beloved hero's betrayal - the loudest story wrestling tells.
why_fun: A card that flips alignment mid-run and rewrites its own effect.

name: The Jobber
effect: The designated losers - the Washington Generals lost over thirteen thousand games to the Globetrotters.
why_fun: A card whose job is to lose, and which pays the card that beats it.

name: The Blind Spot
effect: The folding chair behind the referee's back - cheating as choreography.
why_fun: A card that may break one rule while a specific other card is not looking.

name: The Manager
effect: The talker who carries the silent monster's story - this card cues the card beside it.
why_fun: Delegated activation, which the charge system already supports.

name: Brown M and Ms
effect: Van Halen's rider clause existed to test whether venues had actually read the safety requirements.
why_fun: A card that detects whether a blind was read - and warns you if it was not.

name: The Pose
effect: Voguing - battle dance built from magazine poses, frozen glamour as combat.
why_fun: Hold a formation for a refill to score it again.

name: Butoh
effect: The post-war dance of darkness - white-painted, glacially slow, transformative.
why_fun: A card that changes by one small degree every refill and is unrecognisable by the end.

name: Marcel Marceau
effect: Bip, the world's mime - and before that a Resistance member who used mime to keep hidden children silent as he led them to safety.
why_fun: A card that escorts other cards safely past a hazard. One of the five stories worth full flavour text.

name: Edgar Bergen
effect: A ventriloquist who became the number one act on radio - a skill rendered pointless by the medium, and a star anyway.
why_fun: A card whose stated advantage does not apply and which scores regardless.

name: The Throw
effect: Making the voice live somewhere else - cue a card's effect to resolve at a different cell.
why_fun: Relocating an effect without relocating its card.

name: The Nantes Giants
effect: Building-sized marionettes walked through cities by teams of Lilliputians on ropes.
why_fun: A card so large it occupies several cells and is moved by the cards around it.

name: The Statue
effect: The street performer who scores by not moving - this card gains points for every refill it is untouched.
why_fun: The counterweight to a board that rewards constant action.

name: The Stunt Double
effect: Yakima Canutt invented modern stunt craft, including the Ben-Hur chariot race, so that stars could survive their own films.
why_fun: A card that takes a destructive effect in another card's place.

name: Guy Laliberte
effect: A fire-breathing stilt-walker busking in Quebec who built the world's biggest circus and then bought a seat on a rocket.
why_fun: The busker-to-space progression arc, as a leader whose scaling never stops.

name: David Blaine
effect: Buried alive, frozen in ice, forty-four days fasting in a box over the Thames - the hunger artist with a live feed.
why_fun: An endurance card that scores for refills survived doing nothing.

name: Controlled Props
effect: Carson, an ex-magician briefed by Randi, supplied his own props and the spoon-bending did not happen.
why_fun: A card that neutralises a deception card by insisting on its own conditions.

name: Shin Lim
effect: Close-up card magic - just cards - winning the biggest talent show on television.
why_fun: A card with no props, no class synergies and an enormous ceiling.

name: The Golden Buzzer
effect: One judge's press sends an act straight through, with confetti falling.
why_fun: Skip a node and take its reward.

name: The Vocaloid
effect: A synthetic idol whose songs are written by thousands of fans - a performer made of the audience.
why_fun: A card whose effect is assembled from every other card you own.

name: The Flash Mob
effect: Sudden coordinated performance in public space - assembly is the trick.
why_fun: Several token cards appear at once in a formation and vanish after one refill.

name: The 900
effect: Two and a half rotations, which took eleven public failures first.
why_fun: A card that must fail several times before it can succeed, and remembers how many.

name: Competitive Cheer
effect: Basket tosses and human pyramids under judging panels.
why_fun: The castell mechanic, judged - the formation must be held to be scored.

name: Drone Swarm
effect: Thousands of drones replacing fireworks, drawing pictures on the night sky.
why_fun: Props that arrange themselves into a shape above the whole board.

name: Love is in the Bin
effect: The painting that shredded itself the moment it was auctioned, and doubled in value.
why_fun: The Shredder card - self-destructs when sold and pays double for it.

name: Competitive Eating
effect: Technique doubled the hot-dog record overnight - spectacle sport from pure method.
why_fun: A consumption card that gets faster the more it eats.

name: Scare Acting
effect: A seasonal profession built on timing, safety and the art of the near-touch.
why_fun: A card that threatens an adjacent card without ever destroying it, and scores for the fright.

name: Found-Object Percussion
effect: Blue Man Group and Stomp - junk becomes the orchestra.
why_fun: A card that turns every prop card in its line into a scoring instrument.

name: Avalanche filed
effect: After scoring, every card on the board attacks the scoreboard, reducing the goal by the number of cards.
why_fun: The prototype for every goal-manipulating effect, and still the only one.
